This guide shows you how to build a YAML validation from parts that are kept in separate files:
collections of checks, threshold presets, and table definitions. Each part is written once and
selected by name, and any of them can be changed when the validation is run.

The composing is done by [Hydra](https://hydra.cc), which is an optional dependency:

```bash
pip install "pointblank[hydra]"
```

The keys, config groups, and built-in options are listed in the
[YAML Reference](yaml-reference.qmd#composed-configurations).

## Put Shared Checks in a Collection

A check collection is a YAML file with a `steps:` list, written the same way as the steps of any
YAML validation. It goes in a `pointblank/checks/` directory next to your validation configs:

```
config/
├── orders.yaml
└── pointblank/
    └── checks/
        └── ids.yaml
```

```yaml
# config/pointblank/checks/ids.yaml
# @package checks.ids
steps:
  - col_vals_not_null:
      columns: ${vars.id_column}
  - rows_distinct:
      columns_subset: ${vars.id_column}
```

The first line is required. The name after `checks.` identifies the collection and must be
different for each one.

`${vars.id_column}` is replaced by the `id_column` value under `vars` in the config that selects
the collection, so the same checks can be used on tables that name their ID column differently.

## Select Collections in a Validation Config

A validation config selects what it's made of in a `defaults:` list.

```yaml
# config/orders.yaml
defaults:
  - override /pointblank/tbl: small_table
  - override /pointblank/thresholds: standard
  - override /pointblank/checks:
      - ids
  - _self_

vars:
  id_column: a

tbl_name: Orders
steps:
  - col_vals_gt:
      columns: d
      value: 100
```

Each `override` line selects one option of a config group (or a list of them, for
`pointblank/checks`). Here `small_table` and `standard` are options that come with Pointblank, and
`ids` is the collection defined above. Keep `_self_` as the last entry, so that values in this
file take precedence over the selected options.

The steps of the selected collections come first, in the order they're listed, followed by the
`steps:` of the config itself.

Run the config with `hydra_interrogate()`:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

config_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "config"
(config_dir / "pointblank" / "checks").mkdir(parents=True)

(config_dir / "pointblank" / "checks" / "ids.yaml").write_text(
    """# @package checks.ids
steps:
  - col_vals_not_null:
      columns: ${vars.id_column}
  - rows_distinct:
      columns_subset: ${vars.id_column}
"""
)

(config_dir / "orders.yaml").write_text(
    """defaults:
  - override /pointblank/tbl: small_table
  - override /pointblank/thresholds: standard
  - override /pointblank/checks:
      - ids
  - _self_

vars:
  id_column: a

tbl_name: Orders
steps:
  - col_vals_gt:
      columns: d
      value: 100
"""
)
```

```{python}
import pointblank as pb

pb.hydra_interrogate(config_dir / "orders.yaml")
```

## Change a Selection or a Value for One Run

Pass `overrides=` to select a different option of a group, or to set a single value. Overrides
take precedence over what's in the file.

```{python}
pb.hydra_interrogate(
    config_dir / "orders.yaml",
    overrides=[
        "pointblank/thresholds=strict",  # Select another option of a group
        "thresholds.critical=0.5",       # Set one value
        "vars.id_column=b",              # Point the collection at another column
    ],
)
```

A value that isn't in the composed config yet needs a `+` in front (e.g.,
`"+vars.date_column=date"`).

## Add Your Own Tables and Thresholds

Options for the other config groups are files in the directory of that group. Each one starts
with the `# @package` header of its group.

```yaml
# config/pointblank/tbl/orders_prod.yaml
# @package _global_
tbl: data/orders.parquet
```

```yaml
# config/pointblank/thresholds/release.yaml
# @package thresholds
warning: 1
critical: 0.02
```

Select them as `pointblank/tbl: orders_prod` and `pointblank/thresholds: release`. An option
can't have the name of one that's built into Pointblank (such as `strict`).

## Run a Composed Config from the Command Line

`pb run` composes any YAML config that has a `defaults:` list. Overrides follow the file name.

```bash
pb run config/orders.yaml
pb run config/orders.yaml pointblank/thresholds=strict thresholds.critical=0.5
pb run config/orders.yaml vars.id_column=b --fail-on error
```

Quote an override that has brackets, since most shells give them a meaning of their own.

Without a file, the config is made up of the options you select. Use `--config-dir` to say where
your config groups are:

```bash
pb run pointblank/tbl=small_table 'pointblank/checks=[ids]' +vars.id_column=a --config-dir config
```

## See What a Config Composes To

`pb compose` prints the composed config instead of running it:

```bash
pb compose config/orders.yaml pointblank/thresholds=strict
```

In Python, `hydra_compose()` returns it as a dictionary:

```{python}
import yaml

composed = pb.hydra_compose(config_dir / "orders.yaml", overrides=["pointblank/thresholds=strict"])

print(yaml.safe_dump(composed, sort_keys=False))
```

The result is a plain YAML config with nothing left to compose. If you save it to a file, it
runs with `yaml_interrogate()` or `pb run` on a machine that doesn't have Hydra installed, and
it can be reviewed as the full definition of what a run checks.

## Keep Config Groups in Another Directory

Config groups are looked up in the directory of the validation config. To use groups that are
somewhere else, pass that directory as `config_dir=` (or `--config-dir` on the command line):

```python
pb.hydra_interrogate("orders.yaml", config_dir="shared/config")
```

To make check collections available to every project that installs a package, see
[Sharing Checks in a Package](sharing-checks-in-a-package.qmd).

## Use a Collection in Python Code

`hydra_steps()` returns the steps of one collection as a `Steps` object, which you can add to a
validation that's written in Python. Give the collection's variables as `vars=`.

```{python}
id_checks = pb.hydra_steps("ids", vars={"id_column": "a"}, config_dir=config_dir)

(
    pb.Validate(data=pb.load_dataset("small_table"))
    .add_steps(id_checks)
    .col_vals_gt(columns="d", value=100)
    .interrogate()
)
```

## Use Collections in a Contract

A contract file with a `defaults:` list is composed when it's read with `Contract.from_yaml()`.
Write the contract's fields at the top level of the file:

```yaml
# config/orders_contract.yaml
defaults:
  - override /pointblank/thresholds: strict
  - override /pointblank/checks:
      - ids
  - _self_

vars:
  id_column: order_id

name: orders
version: "1.0.0"
steps:
  - col_vals_gt:
      columns: amount
      value: 0
```

```python
orders_contract = pb.Contract.from_yaml("config/orders_contract.yaml")
```

## Use Collections in a Pipeline

A pipeline file with a `defaults:` list is composed when it's read with `Pipeline.from_yaml()`.
A pipeline has two contracts, so each one names the selected collections it uses in a `checks:`
list. The name of a collection is the one in its `# @package checks.<name>` header.

```yaml
# config/orders_pipeline.yaml
defaults:
  - override /pointblank/thresholds: strict
  - override /pointblank/checks:
      - ids
  - _self_

vars:
  id_column: order_id

pipeline:
  label: Orders
source:
  name: raw_orders
  checks: [ids]
target:
  name: orders
  checks: [ids]
  steps:
    - col_vals_gt:
        columns: amount
        value: 0
```

```python
orders_pipeline = pb.Pipeline.from_yaml("config/orders_pipeline.yaml")
```

The steps of a contract's collections come before its own `steps:`. Every selected collection
has to be used by at least one of the two contracts.

## Use Python Objects in a Config

To use a Python object as a value (a table, a preprocessing function, a custom check), write a
mapping with a `_target_` key. The target is the import path of a callable, and the other keys
are its arguments.

```yaml
tbl:
  _target_: polars.read_parquet
  source: data/orders.parquet

steps:
  - row_count_match:
      count: 5
      pre:
        _target_: polars.DataFrame.head
        _partial_: true
        n: 5
```

Here `tbl` is what `polars.read_parquet("data/orders.parquet")` returns. With
`_partial_: true` the callable isn't called, so `pre` is the function
`polars.DataFrame.head` with `n=5` filled in.

A target is imported and called whenever the config is run. Only run composed configs that you
trust, as you would a Python script.

## Allow Python Code

Python code in `python:` blocks is handled as it is in any YAML config: it isn't run unless you
pass `allow_python=True` to `hydra_interrogate()` or use `pb run --allow-python`. See
[Allowing Python Code to Run](yaml-validation-workflows.qmd#allowing-python-code-to-run). This
doesn't apply to `_target_`, which needs no permission.
